endorsements.quote: Addressing the ASR equity gap rather than treating it as an afterthought requires conducting subgroup analyses by context-specific axes of linguistic variation, including accent, dialect, and professional characteristics as suggested [ 1 ], and disaggregated reporting on adoption, dropout, and equity metrics of ASR performance.

unlisted_practices: Treat documentation as a heterogeneous bundle of authoring, reviewing, retrieving, and verifying activities, each with distinct satisfaction and error profiles, when evaluating AI scribes.
Define and validate end-user-defined anchor utilities for AI scribes, such as time savings, reduced interruptions, or privacy trade-offs, rather than pursuing diffuse improvement.
Report equity testing of ASR performance, disaggregated by speaker characteristics, as a standard reporting expectation rather than a caveat.
Report AI scribe adoption and dropout disaggregated by workforce characteristics such as age, language of origin, career stage, and prior digital experience.
Conduct longitudinal implementation studies of AI scribes lasting at least 12 months, anchored in an implementation science framework.
Investigate privacy and confidentiality protocols for bedside dictation with AI scribes.
Study whether AI scribe-related reductions in interruptions translate into measurable reductions in nursing error, omission, or delay.

screen.reason: This is an invited commentary on an empirical study (Schwabe et al.) discussing implementation considerations, equity, and evaluation frameworks for AI scribes in nursing.
